Now an end-to-end check against a real local server.

`WeatherClient.get` in `weather.py` now tries up to 3 times when the server returns 503, waiting longer before each retry.

- **What gets retried:** only an HTTP 503. Any other HTTP error (for example 404) is raised straight away. Timeouts and connection errors are also raised straight away, since you only asked about 503.
- **Backoff:** the wait doubles each time, starting at `backoff` (0.5s by default), so 0.5s then 1s before the last try.
- **Settings:** two new constructor arguments, `max_attempts=3` and `backoff=0.5`. Existing calls work without changes.
- **When all tries fail:** the last 503 error is raised as usual. The earlier error responses are closed before the client waits and tries again.

I ran it against a real local HTTP server with `backoff=0.05`; no test file was added to the repo.

| Server behaviour | Result | Requests | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 straight away | JSON returned | 1 | 0.01s |
| 503, 503, then 200 | JSON returned | 3 | 0.15s |
| 503 every time | `HTTPError 503` raised | 3 | 0.15s |
| 404 | `HTTPError 404` raised | 1 | 0.00s |

The 0.15s total matches the expected waits of 0.05s + 0.10s.
